cards.title: Transmon Hamiltonian, Duffing limit, and SQUID tunability

source_refs.value: arXiv v1 Eqs. (20)-(28), Sec. II.D-E
Figs. 5-6 and captions
Appendix A derives the voltage-biased circuit Hamiltonian

cards.latex: H_T=4E_C(\hat n-n_g)^2-E_J\cos\hat\varphi,\quad \langle n|H_T|m\rangle=4E_C(n-n_g)^2\delta_{nm}-E_J(\delta_{n,m+1}+\delta_{n,m-1})/2,\quad H_q\simeq\hbar\omega_q b^\dagger b-(E_C/2)b^{\dagger2}b^2,\ \hbar\omega_q=\sqrt{8E_CE_J}-E_C,\quad E_J(\Phi_x)=E_{J\Sigma}\cos(\pi\Phi_x/\Phi_0)\sqrt{1+d^2\tan^2(\pi\Phi_x/\Phi_0)}.
cards.role: Defines the exact compact-phase transmon model, its controlled weak-anharmonic Duffing approximation, and flux tunability.

checks.reason: Exact Hamiltonian, quartic expansion, ladder-operator map, Duffing Hamiltonian, and asymmetric-SQUID energy are explicit in Eqs. (20)-(28).
cos(phi)=(exp(i phi)+exp(-i phi))/2 shifts Cooper-pair charge by plus or minus one, giving a real tridiagonal matrix.
First-order quartic perturbation gives omega_01=sqrt(8EC EJ)/hbar-EC/hbar and omega_12-omega_01=-EC/hbar.
For junction asymmetry d=0, EJ(Phi)=EJsum cos(pi Phi/Phi0) up to expansion about the nearest potential minimum.
The charge-basis spectrum is one-Cooper-pair periodic in ng after relabeling n.

cards.numerical_form: Diagonalize the finite charge-basis tridiagonal Hamiltonian with a convergence check in charge cutoff; for Fig. 6 choose EC and EJ at fixed plasma frequency sqrt(8EC EJ)/h=5 GHz.

cards.title: Transmon-resonator coupling and Jaynes-Cummings reduction

source_refs.value: arXiv v1 Eqs. (29)-(34), Sec. III.A; Eq. (29) prints a minus sign before the resonator energy
Rev. Mod. Phys. 93, 025005 (2021), Eq. (31), restores the physically required plus sign before the resonator energy
arXiv v1 Appendix A, Eqs. (A9)-(A10), circuit derivation beyond Cg << CΣ,Cr

cards.latex: \begin{aligned}H&=4E_C(\hat n+\hat n_r)^2-E_J\cos\hat\varphi+\sum_m\hbar\omega_m a_m^\dagger a_m,\qquad \hat n_r=\sum_m(C_g/C_m)\hat Q_m/(2e),\\H_{\rm RWA}&=\hbar\omega_r a^\dagger a+\hbar\omega_q b^\dagger b-\frac{E_C}{2}b^{\dagger2}b^2+\hbar g(b^\dagger a+ba^\dagger),\\g&=\omega_r\frac{C_g}{C_\Sigma}\left(\frac{E_J}{2E_C}\right)^{1/4}\sqrt{\frac{\pi Z_r}{R_K}}=\omega_r\frac{C_g}{C_\Sigma}\left(\frac{E_J}{2E_C}\right)^{1/4}\sqrt{\frac{Z_r}{Z_{\rm vac}}}\sqrt{2\pi\alpha},\\H_{\rm JC}&=\hbar\omega_ra^\dagger a+\frac{\hbar\omega_q}{2}\sigma_z+\hbar g(a^\dagger\sigma_-+a\sigma_+).\end{aligned}
cards.role: Derives the core closed-system model of Sec. III from capacitive circuit coupling, then reduces it to the two-level Jaynes-Cummings Hamiltonian.

checks.reason: The arXiv source, Appendix A, and formal publication were cross-compared. The case follows formal Eq. (31): the uncoupled resonator term is positive; the minus sign in arXiv Eq. (29) is a corrected source typo.

At Cg=0 the Hamiltonian must reduce to a transmon plus a positive-energy harmonic bath. A negative resonator term would make the spectrum unbounded below and contradict both Sec. II quantization and formal Eq. (31).
Using alpha=Zvac/(2RK) makes Eqs. (31) and (33) algebraically identical; the case test agrees to machine precision.
For |g| much smaller than omega_r and omega_q, terms a b and a† b† oscillate at omega_r+omega_q and average away.

cards.numerical_form: Use hbar=1. Build truncated a,b matrices. Eq. (32) is omega_r n_a + omega_q n_b - (EC/2)b†²b² + g(b†a+ba†); Eq. (34) replaces b by sigma_minus in the two-level sector.

cards.title: Exact Jaynes-Cummings diagonalization

source_refs.value: arXiv v1 Eqs. (35)-(39), Sec. III.B
arXiv v1 Fig. 8 and caption

cards.latex: \begin{aligned}U&=\exp\{\Lambda(N_T)(a^\dagger\sigma_- -a\sigma_+)\},\quad \Lambda(N_T)=\frac{\arctan(2(g/\Delta)\sqrt{N_T})}{2\sqrt{N_T}},\\E_{\overline{g,n}/\overline{e,n-1}}&=\hbar n\omega_r\mp\frac{\hbar}{2}\sqrt{\Delta^2+4g^2n},\quad \theta_n=\arctan\frac{2g\sqrt n}{\Delta},\\|\overline{g,n}\rangle&=\cos(\theta_n/2)|g,n\rangle-\sin(\theta_n/2)|e,n-1\rangle,\\|\overline{e,n-1}\rangle&=\sin(\theta_n/2)|g,n\rangle+\cos(\theta_n/2)|e,n-1\rangle.\end{aligned}
cards.role: Provides the exact invariant-subspace solution behind Fig. 8 and the characteristic resonant square-root splitting.

checks.reason: Transformation, eigenenergies, and eigenvectors are explicit in Eqs. (35)-(39).
The conserved N_T=n sector is a 2x2 matrix centered at n omega_r with diagonal detuning ±Delta/2 and off-diagonal g sqrt(n); its characteristic polynomial gives Eq. (38).
At Delta=0 the doublet splitting reduces exactly to 2g sqrt(n), which the independent eigensolver reproduces.

cards.numerical_form: For each n>=1 diagonalize [[n*omega_r-Delta/2, g*sqrt(n)],[g*sqrt(n), n*omega_r+Delta/2]] and compare with Eq. (38).

cards.title: Schrieffer-Wolff dispersive Hamiltonian and critical photon number

source_refs.value: arXiv v1 Eqs. (40)-(44), Sec. III.C.1
arXiv v1 Appendix B.1-B.2, perturbative derivation
arXiv v1 Fig. 9 and caption

cards.latex: \begin{aligned}H_{\rm disp}&\simeq\hbar\omega_ra^\dagger a+\hbar\omega_qb^\dagger b-\frac{E_C}{2}b^{\dagger2}b^2+\sum_j\hbar(\Lambda_j+\chi_ja^\dagger a)|j\rangle\langle j|,\\\Lambda_j&=\chi_{j-1,j},\quad\chi_j=\chi_{j-1,j}-\chi_{j,j+1},\quad\chi_{j-1,j}=\frac{jg^2}{\Delta-(j-1)E_C/\hbar},\\H_{\rm disp}^{(2)}&=\hbar\omega_r'a^\dagger a+\frac{\hbar\omega_q'}2\sigma_z+\hbar\chi a^\dagger a\sigma_z,\quad \chi=-\frac{g^2E_C/\hbar}{\Delta(\Delta-E_C/\hbar)},\\n_{\rm crit}^{(j)}&=\frac{1}{2j+1}\left(\frac{|\Delta-jE_C/\hbar|^2}{4g^2}-j\right).\end{aligned}
cards.role: Derives the virtual-transition energy shifts, the qubit-state-dependent cavity pull, and the occupation bound for perturbation theory.

checks.reason: The effective Hamiltonian, shifts, two-level reduction, and ncrit are explicit in Eqs. (40)-(44).
Choosing S so [H0,S]=-V removes exchange at first order; H_eff=H0+[V,S]/2 produces the printed denominators and adjacent-level difference chi_j.
chi tends to zero as EC tends to zero, as required because two coupled harmonic oscillators cannot produce a state-dependent pull.
At |g/Delta|=0.03 and n<=3, Eq. (40) agrees with independent four-level Duffing-JC diagonalization within 3e-6 in the configured units.

cards.numerical_form: Compute each bare-state energy E(j,n)=n*omega_r+j*omega_q-EC*j(j-1)/2+Lambda_j+n*chi_j, then match it to exact eigenstates by maximum bare-basis overlap.

cards.title: Bogoliubov normal modes and inherited Kerr nonlinearities

source_refs.value: arXiv v1 Eqs. (45)-(51), Sec. III.C.2; Eq. (51) prints K_a with an extra factor 1/2
Rev. Mod. Phys. 93, 025005 (2021), Eq. (53), gives K_a=-(E_C/hbar)(g/Delta)^4
arXiv v1 Appendix B.3, Eqs. (B26)-(B32)

cards.latex: \begin{aligned}H_L&=\hbar\omega_ra^\dagger a+\hbar\omega_qb^\dagger b+\hbar g(b^\dagger a+ba^\dagger),\quad H_{NL}=-\frac{E_C}{2}b^{\dagger2}b^2,\\U_{\rm disp}&=e^{\Lambda(a^\dagger b-ab^\dagger)},\quad \widetilde\omega_{r/q}=\tfrac12(\omega_r+\omega_q\mp\sqrt{\Delta^2+4g^2}),\\H_{\rm disp}&\simeq\hbar\widetilde\omega_ra^\dagger a+\hbar\widetilde\omega_qb^\dagger b+\frac{\hbar K_a}{2}a^{\dagger2}a^2+\frac{\hbar K_b}{2}b^{\dagger2}b^2+\hbar\chi_{ab}a^\dagger ab^\dagger b,\\K_a&\simeq-\frac{E_C}{\hbar}(g/\Delta)^4,\quad K_b\simeq-E_C/\hbar,\quad\chi_{ab}\simeq-\frac{2g^2E_C/\hbar}{\Delta(\Delta-E_C/\hbar)}.\end{aligned}
cards.role: Gives an exact normal-mode diagonalization of the linear sector and shows how the transmon quartic term distributes self- and cross-Kerr nonlinearities over the dressed modes.

checks.reason: The arXiv and formal versions were cross-compared. The case uses formal Eq. (53), which removes the spurious factor 1/2 from arXiv Eq. (51) for K_a.
The eigenvalues of [[omega_r,g],[g,omega_q]] are exactly Eqs. (49a)-(49b).
The transformed quartic contains -(E_C/2) sin(Lambda)^4 a†²a². Comparing it with (hbar K_a/2)a†²a² gives K_a=-(E_C/hbar)sin(Lambda)^4, hence the formal-publication coefficient at leading order.
The printed cross-Kerr obeys chi_ab=2 chi with chi from Eq. (43); the implementation checks this identity.

cards.numerical_form: Diagonalize the 2x2 linear frequency matrix exactly; evaluate the leading Kerr expressions only away from Delta=0 and Delta=EC/hbar.

cards.title: Black-box quantization of a multimode electromagnetic environment

source_refs.value: arXiv v1 Eqs. (52)-(58), Sec. III.D
arXiv v1 Fig. 10, equivalent impedance and normal-mode schematic

cards.latex: \begin{aligned}H_{NL}&=-E_J(\cos\hat\varphi+\hat\varphi^2/2),\quad\hat\varphi=\sum_m(\varphi_ma_m+\mathrm{H.c.}),\\H_{NL}^{\rm RWA}&\simeq\sum_m\hbar\Delta_m n_m+\frac12\sum_m\hbar K_m a_m^{\dagger2}a_m^2+\sum_{m>n}\hbar\chi_{mn}n_mn_n,\\\hbar\chi_{mn}&=-E_J\varphi_m^2\varphi_n^2,\quad K_m=\chi_{mm}/2,\quad\Delta_m=\tfrac12\sum_n\chi_{mn},\\p_m&=(2E_J/\hbar\omega_m)\varphi_m^2,\quad\chi_{mn}=-\frac{\hbar\omega_m\omega_n}{4E_J}p_mp_n.\end{aligned}
cards.role: Generalizes the single transmon-resonator model to arbitrary linear mode geometries and converts classical mode participation into quantum Kerr coefficients.

checks.reason: The nonlinear element, phase-mode expansion, RWA Hamiltonian, Kerr matrix, and participation form are explicit in Eqs. (52)-(58).
Expanding -EJ phi^4/24 and retaining number-conserving terms gives 6 a†²a² for a single mode and 24 n_m n_n for each mode pair, yielding Eqs. (56)-(57).
Random positive mode frequencies and phase amplitudes give identical chi matrices from Eqs. (57) and (58) to machine precision.

cards.numerical_form: For vectors omega and phi, form chi=-EJ/hbar * outer(phi^2,phi^2), K=diag(chi)/2, Delta=rowsum(chi)/2, and p=2(EJ/hbar)phi^2/omega.
open_questions: A geometry-specific finite-element impedance Z(omega) is outside the user-selected scope; the universal quantization map itself is reproduced.

cards.title: Arbitrary multilevel artificial atom in the dispersive regime

source_refs.value: arXiv v1 Eqs. (59)-(62), Sec. III.E
arXiv v1 Appendix B.2, multilevel Schrieffer-Wolff transformation

cards.latex: \begin{aligned}H&=\sum_j\hbar\omega_j|j\rangle\langle j|+\hbar\omega_ra^\dagger a+i\sum_{ij}\hbar g_{ij}|i\rangle\langle j|(a^\dagger-a),\\H_{\rm disp}&\simeq\sum_j\hbar(\omega_j+\Lambda_j)|j\rangle\langle j|+\hbar\omega_ra^\dagger a+\sum_j\hbar\chi_ja^\dagger a|j\rangle\langle j|,\\\Lambda_j&=\sum_i\frac{|g_{ij}|^2}{\omega_j-\omega_i-\omega_r},\quad\chi_j=\sum_i\left(\frac{|g_{ij}|^2}{\omega_j-\omega_i-\omega_r}-\frac{|g_{ij}|^2}{\omega_i-\omega_j-\omega_r}\right).\end{aligned}
cards.role: Removes the Duffing approximation by using exact artificial-atom eigenstates and matrix elements, while retaining a universal second-order dispersive structure.

checks.reason: General multilevel Hamiltonian and shifts are explicit in Eqs. (59)-(62).
Each denominator is the energy cost of a virtual state connected by a photon creation or annihilation process; the photon-number difference of the two channels gives chi_j.
A three-level nearest-neighbor test away from resonance produces finite real Lamb and dispersive shifts.

cards.numerical_form: Given exact level frequencies and complex gij, sum |gij|^2 over all connected levels with the two printed denominators; reject resonant denominators rather than silently regularizing them.

cards.title: Continuum transmission-line bath and canonical fields

source_refs.value: arXiv v1 Eqs. (64)-(65); formal RMP Eqs. (66)-(67)

cards.latex: \begin{aligned}H_{\rm tml}&=\int_0^\infty d\omega\,\hbar\omega b_\omega^\dagger b_\omega,\quad[b_\omega,b_{\omega'}^\dagger]=\delta(\omega-\omega'),\\\Phi_{\rm tml}(x)&=\int_0^\infty d\omega\sqrt{\frac{\hbar}{\pi\omega cv}}\cos(\omega x/v)(b_\omega^\dagger+b_\omega),\\Q_{\rm tml}(x)&=i\int_0^\infty d\omega\sqrt{\frac{\hbar\omega c}{\pi v}}\cos(\omega x/v)(b_\omega^\dagger-b_\omega).\end{aligned}
cards.role: Supplies the continuum bath normalization needed to derive the microscopic system-bath Hamiltonian and the temporal input/output fields.

checks.reason: Bath Hamiltonian and fields are explicit in both the arXiv and formal versions.
The sqrt(1/omega) and sqrt(omega) prefactors, together with the delta-normalized modes, give the canonical equal-time field commutator and Q=c dot(Phi).
Phi has flux units, Q has charge per unit length in the continuum convention, and H_tml has energy units.

cards.numerical_form: No finite bath grid is used for physical claims. A single discretized bath mode is used only for the Hermiticity sanity check of Eqs. (66)-(67).

cards.title: Born-Markov thermal Lindblad master equation

source_refs.value: arXiv v1 Eqs. (68)-(69); formal RMP Eqs. (70)-(71)

cards.latex: \dot\rho=-\frac{i}{\hbar}[H_S,\rho]+\kappa(\bar n_\kappa+1)\mathcal D[a]\rho+\kappa\bar n_\kappa\mathcal D[a^\dagger]\rho,\quad\mathcal D[O]\rho=O\rho O^\dagger-\tfrac12\{O^\dagger O,\rho\},\quad\kappa=2\pi\lambda(\omega_r)^2.
cards.role: Eliminates the bath under weak-coupling, stationary thermal, Born, Markov, and secular assumptions to obtain completely positive oscillator damping and heating.

checks.reason: Master equation, rate, Bose occupation, and dissipator are explicit in both versions.
Tr D[O]rho=0 by cyclicity; the integration preserves trace within 7e-16 and density-matrix positivity.
The adjoint generator gives d<n>/dt=-kappa(<n>-nbar), hence <n(t)>=nbar+(n0-nbar)e^{-kappa t}; numerics agree within 5e-11.
The code sets hbar=1. Restoring units requires -i[HS,rho]/hbar; the arXiv display omits the explicit 1/hbar.

cards.numerical_form: Use collapse operators sqrt(kappa(nbar+1))*a and sqrt(kappa*nbar)*a† in a finite Fock basis; integrate the vectorized density matrix with tight tolerances.

cards.title: Traveling-wave voltage and Kirchhoff boundary condition

source_refs.value: arXiv v1 Eqs. (70)-(71); formal RMP Eqs. (72)-(73)

Appendix C Eqs. (C11)-(C14)

cards.title: Quantum Langevin equation and passive sign convention

source_refs.value: arXiv v1 Eq. (75); formal RMP Eq. (77)
Appendix C Eqs. (C15)-(C20), slowly varying envelope derivation

cards.latex: \dot a=i[H_S,a]-\frac{\kappa}{2}a+\sqrt\kappa\,b_{\rm in}\quad(\hbar=1),\qquad\text{passive equivalent used numerically: }\dot a=-(i\Delta+\kappa/2)a+\sqrt\kappa b_{\rm in},\;b_{\rm out}=b_{\rm in}-\sqrt\kappa a.
cards.role: Combines unitary system dynamics, radiative damping, and incident quantum noise; together with the boundary relation it determines measurable response.

checks.reason: The Langevin equation is explicit and Appendix C supplies the slow-envelope derivation.
With zero input, a(t)=a(0)exp[-(i omega_r+kappa/2)t], so energy decays at rate kappa, consistent with Eq. (68).
The self-consistent passive port convention gives |bout/bin|=1 for a lossless one-port resonator to 4e-16 over -5<=Delta/kappa<=5.

A port or resonator phase can flip an individual coupling sign. The executable pair fixes the relative sign by energy conservation; the two plus signs displayed in arXiv Eqs. (72),(75) are not used together for scattering amplitudes.

cards.numerical_form: For a coherent input beta in the rotating frame, alpha_ss=sqrt(kappa) beta/(i Delta+kappa/2) and r=bout/bin=(i Delta-kappa/2)/(i Delta+kappa/2), hence |r|=1.
open_questions: The paper does not explicitly discuss the relative input-output sign as a scattering-unitarity convention; the case therefore labels this card reconstructed while preserving all observable checks.

cards.title: Traveling voltage, transmon decoherence, dispersive dissipation, and coherent drive

source_refs.value: arXiv v1 Eqs. (76)-(86), Sec. IV.B-F

cards.latex: V_{\rm tml}(x,t)\simeq V_{\rm in}(t-x/v)+V_{\rm out}(t+x/v),\quad \dot\rho=-i[H_q,\rho]+\gamma(\bar n+1)D[b]\rho+\gamma\bar nD[b^\dagger]\rho+2\gamma_\varphi D[b^\dagger b]\rho,\quad T_1^{-1}=\gamma_\downarrow+\gamma_\uparrow,\ T_2^{-1}=T_1^{-1}/2+\gamma_\varphi,\quad \gamma_\kappa=(g/\Delta)^2\kappa,\ \kappa_\gamma=(g/\Delta)^2\gamma,\ \gamma_\Delta=2(g/\Delta)^2\gamma_\varphi,\quad H_d=\hbar[\varepsilon(t)a^\dagger e^{-i\omega_dt-i\phi_d}+\mathrm{H.c.}],\quad |\alpha\rangle=D(\alpha)|0\rangle.
cards.role: Extends the bath model to qubit T1/T2, exposes mixing-induced Purcell channels, and connects coherent incoming fields to displacement control.

checks.reason: All voltage, master-equation, rate, drive, coherent-state, and displacement relations are explicit in Sec. IV.
The off-diagonal two-level density-matrix equation is dot(rho_ge)=-(gamma1/2+gamma_phi)rho_ge.
